title: Reservoir routing ships as default vLLM and SGLang serving knob by H2 2026
body: By H2 2026 the Reservoir Routing stateful Mixture-of-Experts primitive — first published Wednesday on arxiv.org/abs/2605.10142 by Stanford CRFM PhD candidate Aryaman Arora and DeepMind senior research scientist Aakanksha Chowdhery — lands as a default-tunable serving-stack knob in both vLLM and SGLang on frontier-class MoE backbones, with the router-state-bank caching expert-selection trajectories across multi-turn agentic conversations rather than recomputing routing at every token. The paper reports a 4.1 percentage-point SWE-Bench Verified uplift on the 145B MoE backbone (Qwen3 MoE 60B uplifted with the Tsinghua KEG Lab MiniMax M2.7 235B port from Unsloth v2026.5.26), landing the augmented backbone at 78.7 against the published 74.6 baseline on tool-use chains exceeding eight tool calls, while reducing per-turn router-compute cost by 31.4 percent on an 8x H100 SXM5 reference node. Two early independent Hacker News reproductions on Lambda Labs rentals already landed throughput numbers inside 2.5 percent of the Stanford-DeepMind reference sheet inside the first day, and Simon Willison flagged the primitive as the first credible reservoir-style routing innovation shipped against a contemporary frontier-class MoE backbone. The structural force is that once a router-state-bank primitive lands at a 4.1pp end-to-end agentic benchmark uplift with a 31.4 percent per-turn router-compute reduction on a frontier-class MoE backbone, gets reproduced inside hours on commodity rental fleets, and pairs naturally with the just-shipped vLLM v0.11.5-rc1 expert-fused-router pass already serving Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B at 22,140 tokens per second, the serving-stack maintainer cohort has the engineering envelope to fold the primitive into the next minor release cycle and the agentic-workload tenants on Together AI plus Fireworks AI plus the Hugging Face hosted-endpoint cohort create the demand-side pull. The most likely landing is that by H2 2026 both vLLM and SGLang ship reservoir-routing as a serving-time tunable knob on their MoE backends, with at least one hyperscaler-managed inference tier (Together AI, Fireworks AI, Anyscale, or one of the Big-3 hyperscaler managed-inference services) exposing it as a customer-facing configuration option behind the routing-state-bank capacity slider. Bear case is that one of the two projects ships a competing fused-routing-context primitive that splits the upstream consensus before convergence, slipping cross-project default availability into Q1 2027; absent that fragmentation, H2 2026 lands reservoir routing as a default-tunable serving-stack knob across both vLLM and SGLang.

reasoning.because: ArXiv 2605.10142 ships reservoir routing: 4.1pp SWE-Bench uplift, 31.4 percent router-compute cut.
reasoning.given: vLLM v0.11.5-rc1 expert-fused-router pass + two Lambda Labs reproductions inside 2.5 percent.
reasoning.so_that: vLLM and SGLang fold reservoir-routing into MoE backends as a serving-time knob with a hosted-tier exposing it.
reasoning.landing: By H2 2026; vLLM + SGLang default it; one hosted-inference tier surfaces it.
reasoning.plain_language: A new trick helps big AI models remember which expert to use across long chats, so popular AI serving tools will soon ship it.

summary: Stanford CRFM and DeepMind shipped Reservoir Routing Wednesday on arxiv (2605.10142), a stateful MoE router-state-bank primitive landing a 4.1pp SWE-Bench Verified uplift and 31.4 percent router-compute cut on a 145B MoE backbone. By H2 2026 vLLM and SGLang ship it as a default-tunable serving knob.
